message.content: {"name":"build_houses_or_hotel","parameters":{"build_plan":[{"space_key":"ATLANTIC_AVENUE","kind":"HOUSE","count":1},{"space_key":"VENTNOR_AVENUE","kind":"HOUSE","count":1},{"space_key":"MARVIN_GARDENS","kind":"HOUSE","count":1}],"public_message":"Yellow's open. One house each.","private_thought":"Built 1 house on each yellow ($450). Cash $149. Past light-blue hotels for ~4 rolls; p2 on Tennessee hits yellow 11/36 this turn so houses earn immediately. 1-house rent is the required step toward the $800 3-house tier — hoarding dies to p3 hotels before I ever afford $1350. If next roll is a $200 RR (2/36), sell one house ($75) and survive. Never sell NY, PP, Med, or yellow. No trade that arms p1 orange/dark blue or gives away yellow."}}
message.reasoning:
I'm ready to play Monopoly.

I'm p4 with $599 and a yellow monopoly. I just paid $10 rent to p3. p1 has $48 and owns all four railroads.

p2 has $76 and GOOJF. p3 is in jail with $3226 and full hotels on light blue. The bank has 32 houses and 9 hotels. I'm considering building evenly on my yellow monopoly.

I'm calculating the even-building costs. One house on each yellow property costs $150, leaving $449. Two houses cost $300, leaving $299. Three houses cost $450, leaving $149. I'm also recalling the rent values for these properties.

I've mapped the board positions. I'm now weighing the risk of p3's light blue hotels against the rent returns from my yellow properties.

I'm on States (space 13). This is my post-roll phase after paying rent. Next players will move before I roll again.

The turn order is p1, p2, p3, then p4. After I end my turn, p1 will move next. p3 is in jail with $3226 and zero jail turns; they can pay the $50 bail to leave immediately.

I'm calculating which players can land on my yellow properties before I roll again. p1 on Virginia cannot reach them, since the maximum roll of 12 is too small. p2 on Tennessee could potentially hit them.

p2 has roughly a 30% chance of landing on my yellow properties before I roll again. p3 cannot reach them from jail even if they leave immediately. This makes the decision to build houses more urgent.

I'm checking what spaces I can land on from States. The nearest ones are Penn RR, New York, and the railroads. Light blue hotels require a 33-space trip around the board, so I cannot reach them this roll.

I'm now assessing my next roll from States. The biggest immediate threat is a roll of 2 or 12, which would hit Penn RR or B&O for $200. Other properties on that path pay only $18 to $20. I'm also considering the risk of drawing a bad Chance card, such as being sent to Boardwalk while it's mortgaged.

The light-blue hotel threat is deferred until I go around the board. Building three houses would leave me with only $149, which is too little to cover a $200 railroad rent if I roll 2 or 12. I'm now checking the mortgage values of my other properties to see what I could sell.

I cannot mortgage my yellow properties while they have houses on them. If I build three houses and then roll a 2 or 12, I would sell the houses for half price to pay the $200 railroad rent. That leaves me with about $174, but I lose the houses entirely.

Building two houses instead leaves me with $299. I can pay the $200 railroad rent and still keep the houses. This is the safer option.

I'm now calculating the exact rent values for two houses on each yellow property. Atlantic would pay $330, Ventnor $360, and Marvin $360. I'm weighing which two properties should receive the houses to maximize expected rent from p2 landing there.

The expected rent gain from p2 landing on my yellow properties is only about $17. That is far below the $300 cost of building two houses. The houses will persist for future turns, but this single roll offers little return. I need to develop my yellow monopoly long-term to threaten p3's light blue hotels.

I'm now deciding how many houses to build. Three houses would cost $450 and leave me with only $149.

I'm now comparing the three house options. One house leaves $449 but yields weak rent. Two houses leaves $299 and can absorb a $200 railroad hit with $99 left over. Three houses would leave only $149, forcing me to sell a house for $75 and mortgage Park Place just to pay the $200 rent. I'll build two houses for now. The long-term goal is to reach three houses so rent jumps above $800.

I checked the full yellow rent schedule. One house yields $110 to $120, which p3 can easily afford. Two houses yield $330 to $360, still manageable for them. The real jump is at three houses, where rent reaches $800 to $850. I cannot build three houses yet because I only have $599 and need $1350. I will build one house on each property now and continue working toward three.

I'm now weighing the risk of drawing a bad Chance card. From States, the nearest railroad is B&O at space 25. If p1 owns it with four railroads, paying double would cost $400. That is far more than the $200 rent from a regular roll. I also noted that landing on p2's properties would only cost about $18.

I'm now weighing the full range of Chance cards. A double-railroad hit is rare, and a poor-tax or repair bill would be manageable. The real value of building houses is for future turns, not this single roll.

p2 is positioned directly before my yellow properties. They have an 11/36 chance of landing there before I roll again. Building houses now would let me collect rent from them immediately.

The expected rent from p2 landing on my yellow properties with one house each is only about $21 this turn. That is far below the $450 cost of building them. The real value of these houses is their persistence across future turns, since yellow spaces are high-traffic after jail.

I'm now calculating the long-term payback of building houses. With one house on each yellow property, I might collect roughly $40 to $50 extra per opponent circuit. Three opponents and several circuits later, the $450 cost could amortize.

However, p3's hotels will eventually threaten me. From my current position at space 13, it takes about 33 to 36 spaces to reach Oriental Avenue. That puts me in danger within four or five of my turns.

If I spend $450 on houses now, I'll have only $149 left. That is too little to cover a hotel without selling houses and mortgaging. I need to either have more cash or be able to mortgage before that danger zone arrives.

I mapped the turn-by-turn timeline. I will reach the light-blue danger zone in about four or five of my turns. During that window, other players will each take several turns. Passing GO once around turn four would add roughly $200. Combined with my current cash, that brings me to about $349. That is still short of the $550 needed to cover a hotel. I am now checking which opponents will actually land on my yellow properties.

p1 can only land on my yellow properties this turn if he rolls a 12, which is unlikely. p2 has an 11/36 chance of paying $110 to $120 from his current position. p3 could reach my yellow properties in about two turns if he leaves jail and rolls well, giving me another rent collection before the light-blue danger zone arrives.

I checked the exact numbers for a hotel hit with only $350 and three houses. Selling the houses for half price would bring cash to $574. That is still $26 short of the Connecticut hotel cost. I would have to mortgage Mediterranean Avenue to survive. I would lose all houses and one property, but I would not go bankrupt.

I cannot afford three houses yet. I need $751 more to reach the $1350 target, and that will take many turns. I am now calculating how much cash I can generate from passing GO twice and collecting rent with partial houses.

I considered building two houses on Atlantic and Ventnor to preserve a larger cash buffer. That would leave $299, cover the $200 railroad rent, and still allow selling the houses for $150 to survive a hotel hit. However, the even-build rule requires one house on every yellow property before any can advance to two. I am now weighing whether the aggressive play of building three houses on all three yellows is the right move.

I am now considering trades with p1, p2, and p3 to complete a second monopoly or acquire cash. I must never sell Mediterranean Avenue, since p3 could then claim it to complete the brown monopoly.

I am now mapping the full board to find viable trades. The pink and red monopolies are split between p2 and p3, so I cannot complete either. The green and dark blue monopolies are also incomplete. p1 wants New York Avenue to finish his orange monopoly, but giving it away would let him claim Boardwalk and complete the best possible set. He previously offered Park Place plus cash for it, and I rejected that trade because it would strengthen his position.

I rejected the trade with p1 because it would leave me cash-poor and fund his dark blue. I considered buying Boardwalk from him to complete that monopoly, but it is mortgaged and costly to unmortgage, so yellow houses are a better use of my money. I also looked at getting the orange set from p1, but he wants Park Place.

I rejected the trade with p1 again because it would arm him with dark blue and orange. Unmortgaging those orange properties costs nearly $200, and I would have to give up Park Place or cash. No trade with p1 is viable without weakening myself. I will not trade yellow or Mediterranean Avenue to p2 either. Buying their incomplete sets would waste my money.

I checked whether p3 or p2 might accept a trade. p3 has no other properties I need, and p2 lacks any yellow properties to offer in return. No viable deals exist right now. I will proceed with building houses.

I will build one house on each yellow property. That costs $450 and leaves me with $149. I checked the risk of landing on a railroad from States. A roll of 2 or 12 lands on the Reading or B&O RR for $200. I can sell one house for $75 to cover that. I would still have $24 left. Other rolls bring little rent.

The risk of a forced house sale is only about eight to ten percent. Building two houses would leave $299, but that would leave Marvin Gardens with zero houses and break the even-build rule. I will build one house on each yellow property instead. That preserves the even distribution and lets me add another layer when cash allows.

I have decided to build three houses on each yellow property. The liquidity hit is manageable, and this aggressive development path is the only way to win.

Hoarding cash is unworkable. Hotel rent will drain my balance before I can afford three houses. Houses act as a half-value insurance piggy bank and a weapon. The expected value of extra rent collected before any liquidation must exceed the 50% haircut.

I will keep my properties unmortgaged so they can be mortgaged later if needed. I will build houses first and then end the turn. I am now preparing the exact JSON payload for the build tool call.

I am now reconsidering the house count. Building only two houses would leave $299, which could cover a $200 railroad rent without selling any buildings. I am also checking whether a Chance card forcing payment to the nearest railroad would double the rent to $400.

The rare Chance card that doubles railroad rent would still leave me $26 short after selling all three houses. A "Chairman of the board" card would cost $150, which is one dollar more than I have, so I would have to sell a house. The probability of either event is only about 0.7%. Overall, building three houses remains acceptable risk.

I compared the expected value of skipping Marvin Gardens' house. The difference is only about four dollars, but building three houses now is still correct because it unlocks the even-build path to two houses on every yellow property.

p3 has no trade leverage while in jail, so I will build houses. I will keep my public message short and non-telegraphing.

function.name: end_turn
function.arguments: {"public_message":"Done for now.","private_thought":"Houses are up. Cash is thin at $149 — do not build more or trade away NY, PP, Med, or yellow. Next roll from States: only real bill is a railroad on 2 or 12 ($200); sell one house if that hits. p3 still the boss with light-blue hotels; win condition is layering yellow to 3 houses before I lap back into them. Stay alive and collect."}
